To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The major, N2- guanine adduct of the carcinogenic, (+)-anti-BPDE can be hydrolyzed in DNA to release the corresponding BPDE-tetraols; (2) The hydrolysis is specific acid catalyze; (3) The hydrolyzed adducts remain covalently bound to the guanine in the DNA.

(1) (+)-anti-BPDE adduct formation is not the only factor determining mutation specificity, since the same adducts in different sequences can have different mutagenic properties, (2) adducts of (+)-antiBPDE at N2-G can be unstable in DNA, and (3) the mutational specificity of (+)-anti BPDE is determined by the relative rates of DNA synthesis past the N2-G adduct, the N10-G adduct, and
the major adduct formed by (+)-anti-BaPDE, N2-Gu, can be unstable in DNA, and that this instability can lead to a decrease in mutation frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of mutagenicity of the carcinogen (+)-anti-BPDE.
the mechanism by which the (+)-anti- diol epoxide, (+)-anti-B[ a]PDE of benzo[ a]pyrene, mutates in the supF gene of plasmid pU3B.
the mechanism of the mutagenesis by a carcinogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major, N2- Gua adduct of (+) anti-B[a]P diol epoxide in double-stranded B-DNA is stable at neutral pH, but can be unstable at low pH.
the (+)-anti-BPDE adduct at N2-guanine in DNA, which is the major BPDE-DNA adduct, is stable at physiological pH, but becomes unstable under conditions of low pH, low Mg2+ and high temperatures.

the major, N2-guanine adducts of (+)-anti-anti-B[a]pyrene-7,8-diol-9,10-epoxide are unstable in DNA at 80 degreesC, and that hydrolysis of these adducts occurs by a mechanism involving specific acid catalysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the N2-Gua (+)-anti-BPDE adduct is stable in single stranded DNA, and in the absence of a divalent cation in double stranded DNA, but is not stable in double stranded DNA in the presence of a divalent metal cation.

the major N2-guanine adduct of (+)anti-B[a]pyrene-7,8-diol-9,10-epoxide (B[a]PDE) in double-stranded plasmid DNA can be unstable, but the mechanism of this hydrolysis is complex and is not simply the hydrolysis of the diol epoxide itself.

the major N2-Gua (+)-anti-BaPDE adduct in double-stranded plasmid DNA is stable to 80 degrees C in the absence of Mg2+ and is not a major mutagenic intermediate in the mutagenesis of supF by (+)-anti-B(a)PDE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N2-Gua major adduct of B[a]PDE can be unstable in DNA, and that adducts are released by simple hydrolysis.
the major, N2-guanine adduct of the anti-diol epoxide of benza[a]pyrene is not always stable in double-stranded, but not single-stranded DNA.
